baseline: analytic roofline, ZERO learned parameters: max(compute_time, memory_time)
why_max_not_min: for a FIXED amount of work the kernel is bounded BELOW by both resources, so the floor is max(...). gpu-sim-u2o.6.6.4 measured min() under-predicting ~100% at every size on this same anchor.

device.name: RTX 5090
device.peak_provenance: spec-sheet figures, NOT measured in this file. A baseline built on an unmeasured peak inherits its uncertainty; the ACHIEVED column in the artifact is measured and is the one to check against.

criterion_1_byte_convention.rule: per-kernel array touches x 4 bytes x n, from the kernel bodies; NEVER a flat 2*n*4

k_saxpy.why: y[j] = alpha * x[j] + y[j] reads x, reads y, writes y

k_copy.why: dst[j] = src[j] reads src, writes dst

k_relu.why: y[j] = x[j] > 0 ? x[j] : 0 reads x, writes y

k_strided_read.why: out[i] = in[i*stride] reads in, writes out

k_scatter_write.why: out[indices[i]] = in[i] reads in, reads indices, writes out

k_random_access.why: reads seeds, reads in[rand], writes out

k_block_sum.why: reads in, writes one partial per block

k_tiled_gemm.why: reads A, reads B, writes C (tiled, so A and B are re-read per tile)

criterion_2_ceiling.membership_rule: largest problem size (HBM-bound), streaming kernels only, both sides uncontended

criterion_3_reconciliation.note: achieved_GBps == bytes_moved/(median/1e6)/1e9 recomputed here from the artifact's own stored fields. A fresh computation would be an identity once both share a helper, which is why the values come from the committed file.

criterion_4_census.warning: families ['gemm', 'reduce'] each rest on ONE kernel, so a per-family figure computed from them is a PER-KERNEL measurement wearing a family label. Report both, and do not describe those families' numbers as family-level evidence.

multipliers.note: compute-bound is NOT MEASURED: no co-tenant effect was recorded for that regime, so its 1.0 is an ASSUMPTION, unlike the two multipliers that were measured. A roofline calibrated on contended cells reads HIGH, because sharing the memory system LOWERS achieved bandwidth. So the bias is quiet: the baseline understates the achievable ceiling rather than failing loudly. Criterion 5.

criterion_5_contention.basis: every anchor family recorded n_other_running=0 on both sides; the queue_state is in the artifact's queue_state_by_family
criterion_5_contention.refusal: is_ceiling_eligible() REFUSES any cell whose contention_state != 'uncontended', so a contended cell cannot quietly become a ceiling

criterion_6_regime_weighting.why: a single global error bar is wrong: the measured co-tenant effect is 2.33x on a memory-bound cell and 1.05-1.19x on a sub-10us one, so the discard threshold must be regime-weighted

headline_finding.my_first_hypothesis_was_wrong: WRONG, and recorded rather than deleted. I expected to find the anchor's ceiling overstated 1.50x, on the reading that it used a flat 2*n*4. CHECKING showed the anchor's saxpy n=2^26 cell already carries 805,306,368 bytes = 3*n*4, which is the CORRECT per-kernel accounting (its commit 734980f is literally 'one byte convention in the file, and the artifact regenerated with it'). The 1.50x figure came from the anchor's PROSE, which still says 2*n*4 -- I believed the prose over the numbers, which is the exact inversion of the standard this lab applies everywhere else.

ceiling_unchanged.difference_is_launch_config_not_bytes: the anchor's ceiling cell is 'saxpy n=67108864 auto/256' and my argmax is 'saxpy n=67108864 auto/1024' -- same kernel, same n, different block size. The 0.6% gap is a launch config difference, NOT a byte correction. The published ceiling STANDS.

two_residual_defects_found.says: 2*n*4 bytes moved (one read + one write, fp32)
two_residual_defects_found.but_the_numbers_use: 3*n*4 for the very cell it describes
two_residual_defects_found.impact: no numerical effect -- the fields are right -- but it is a prose/artifact disagreement of exactly the class gpu-sim-u2o.6.11.1's lint exists to catch, and it misleads the next reader into auditing correct numbers.

two_residual_defects_found.defect: k_scatter_write ALSO credited 2*n*4 but moves 3 arrays
two_residual_defects_found.evidence: out[indices[i]] = in[i] reads in, reads indices, writes out = 3 touches; the anchor carries 2*n*4 for all four scatter_write cells.
two_residual_defects_found.impact: 1.50x on those cells' achieved GB/s; not the ceiling.

two_residual_defects_found.evidence: anchor ceiling_candidates: random_access n=4194304 carries 33,554,432 = 2*n*4, but the body is seed = seeds[i]; idx = seed % n; out[i] = in[idx] -- reads seeds, reads in[rand], writes out = 3 array touches = 3*n*4.
two_residual_defects_found.impact: its achieved_GBps is overstated 1.50x. It does NOT move the memory ceiling, because random_access is not the argmax, but it corrupts any per-family bandwidth figure for the 'access' family -- which is 45 of the 124 cells, the largest family in the anchor.

per_kernel_accounting_check.note: criterion 1 checked as a per-kernel comparison between THIS accounting and the anchor's committed bytes_moved, so agreement and disagreement are both findings rather than assertions

headline_finding.accounting_agrees_on_12_of_21: per-kernel, our accounting agrees with the anchor's committed bytes_moved on 12 of 21 reconciled cells. The 9 disagreements split BOTH WAYS, which is why the check is two-sided: we are more correct on scatter_write and random_access (3 array touches, anchor says 2) and CRUDER on strided_read (we ignore the stride footprint, the anchor deliberately accounts for it). Neither kernel is the ceiling, so the published ceiling is unaffected -- but the anchor's access-family bandwidth figures for scatter and random are 1.50x optimistic, and strided is a different convention rather than a different answer.
headline_finding.what_this_bead_actually_delivers: the baseline itself, with all seven criteria evidenced, plus a verified statement that the published memory ceiling is NOT inflated by a byte-accounting error -- which is a result, and it is the opposite of the one I set out expecting.
